This document records what exists today, shows the real site data flowing through the pipeline, sets out the tech stack and why each piece was chosen, and lines up the build we start next. It is written against your original brief, restated below verbatim in intent.

01The brief

Original requirement

A deterministic + LLM + vision expert that helps contractors draw their plans in a few possible ways, optimising for easier to do, less cost, or a balance of both.

The contractor’s deliverable is a CAD plan — the drawing that shows where their new line runs among everyone else’s. They do not start with that drawing; this tool makes it, or helps them make it. What they start from is the surrounding record: a base survey plus a few PDFs from the other third-party utility owners sharing the same street/space. The new line must sit among the existing ones without affecting them. Access means digging — cheaper when machinery can be used, but crossing another provider’s line forces careful manual work so nothing is broken.

The final output is a finished CAD file, a documented explanation of how to do the work and why each decision was made, and drawings of the alternatives with their explanations — at minimum best cost-wise, best effort-wise, and best balancing the two.

02Where we are

Three things are done, and the one blocker (the CAD base was corrupt on first upload) is cleared.

✓ Research & architecture ✓ Working prototype (3 strategies) ✓ Real site data ingested ✓ DWG recovered & parsed next · fuse into one model

03The real site data

Your three files are the exact input set from the brief: one CAD base plus third-party PDFs, all covering the same stretch of Jalan Bukit Merah. Each was ingested with a tool chosen for faithfulness — true geometry in, no guessing.

3.1 TOPO.dwg — the survey base

The first upload was truncated and unreadable (confirmed independently by two decoders). The re-uploaded file is complete and converts cleanly. It is a real topographic survey in SVY21 coordinates — 2,324 entities across 46 layers, with third-party assets already on typed manhole layers.

S_MH-WD water ×50 S_MH-GAS gas ×21 S_MH-SEW sewer ×15 S_MH-STARHUB telecom ×18 S_ELECTRIC-BOX ×23 S_DRAIN_LINE ×74 S_ROAD/FP_LINE ×243 S_TREE ×228

3.2 Services Plan.pdf — SP power network

Three large-format sheets of the same area at different voltages (230/66 kV, then 6.6/22 kV, shown here). A true vector PDF, so the cable routes, the legend (power / auxiliary / abandoned), the cyan search boundary and the HDD notes all extract exactly — no OCR guesswork.

3.3 ESS Drawing.pdf — multi-utility services

Five matchline sheets detailing every other utility along the corridor. Extraction keys assets by colour and label: GAS×117 (green), LV power (magenta), open drains (cyan), sewer, PE pipes×38, lamp posts, and abandoned runs.

They line up. Base + both PDF sets share one location and (for the DWG) the SVY21 grid, so they can be georeferenced into a single world model — precisely the input the optimiser needs.

04The prototype, on synthetic ground

Ahead of the real data, a runnable prototype already proves the core: it prices every candidate trench on two axes (dollars and effort/risk), enforces clearances as hard constraints, and returns the three strategies the brief asks for. Boring (HDD) is a per-segment method the optimiser can pick.

StrategyLengthCost (S$)Live crossingsBoredRisk
Least cost (open-cut)172 m33,55540 m44
Balanced (trenchless-assisted)172 m33,83508 m0
Least effort (open-cut)194 m35,58800 m0

Figures are from a synthetic scene with placeholder costs; the same engine runs on the real model next. Cost/clearance values must be replaced with PUB / SP / City Energy / IMDA / LTA code figures.

05Tech stack & why — with a product lens

Every choice below is free/open and was picked for faithfulness first. Because this may become a product used by many contractors, the table also flags the licensing and scaling implications — the two things that bite when you move from one engineer’s laptop to a multi-tenant service. The honest headline: the geometry, GIS and optimisation layers are permissively licensed and safe to build a product on; the DWG reader is the one commercial decision to make.

LayerToolWhy it’s hereLicenceProduct implication
DWG → DXFODA File Converter 27.1Reference-grade DWG reader; the only tool that read the real R2018 file.Free binary, closedDecision point — redistribution needs an ODA SDK membership (paid) for a product; keep it isolated behind a conversion service.
DWG (fallback)LibreDWGFully open DWG reader; good for many files.GPL-3.0Copyleft — invoke as a separate CLI process, never link into the product. Failed on this file, so secondary.
PDF render + extractPyMuPDFVector-accurate render and geometry/text extraction.AGPL-3.0 / commercialAGPL is a real constraint for SaaS — plan to swap to pypdfium2 (Apache) + pdfplumber (MIT), or buy the PyMuPDF commercial licence.
DXF read/writeezdxfFull DXF control + faithful rendering; authors the output CAD on SLA layers.MITSafe. Core of both ingest and output.
GeometryShapely / GEOSBuffers (clearance), intersections (crossings), distance.BSD / LGPLSafe. Scales; move heavy work to PostGIS when data grows.
Routing / optimisationNetworkXShortest-path over the weighted cost graph.BSDSafe. Swap for igraph / OR-Tools / pgRouting at city scale.
DrawingsMatplotlibDeterministic plan-view figures for each alternative.PSF/BSD-likeSafe.
Vision + languageClaude (Opus 4.8)Structured extraction from scanned/ambiguous plans; codes→tables; the written method & rationale.APIPer-call cost — cache aggressively; deterministic core stays authoritative so the LLM never sets geometry.
Isolation / runtimeDockerPins the DWG converters and their Qt deps reproducibly; the stdin-pipe pattern works even where the daemon can’t see the disk.ApacheBecomes the per-tenant conversion worker in the product.

Faithfulness, concretely. Both PDFs are vector, so extraction reads the actual drawn geometry rather than OCR-ing a picture of it. The DWG converts through the format’s own reference implementation, then renders with its real ACI colours. Where a source is ever a scan, that is the one place vision/OCR enters — and it stays gated behind a human survey-quality (QL) check before it can constrain a route.

07What we build next

The sequence that turns today’s pieces into the brief’s deliverable on the real site.

1

Fuse into one SVY21 world model

TOPO.dxf as the base; extract SP + ESS utilities to structured geometry (GeoJSON/DXF), georeference the PDFs onto SVY21, tag each line by type, owner and survey quality.

2

Real conflict + cost model

Clearance buffers widened by QL uncertainty; costs/clearances from the actual PUB/SP/City Energy/IMDA/LTA codes of practice, ingested via Claude and checked by a human.

3

Optimise on the real corridor

Run cost / effort / balanced on the merged model, with open-cut vs. HDD per segment; return the Pareto set, not just three points.

4

Finished CAD + LLM narrative

Author the output DWG on SLA layers with the chosen line, chambers and crossings; Claude writes the method statement and decision rationale from the structured result.

5

Productise

Resolve the DWG-licensing decision, move geometry to PostGIS, wrap ingestion in the Docker conversion worker, and template the whole run so any contractor can drop in their files.
